en.AgostinoDescription:
Antonino Agostino, also known as Nino, was born in Palermo on March 29, 1961.
Married to Ida Castelluccio and expecting their first child, he was a police agent based at San Lorenzo station.

He was a lively and loyal boy who fought for a just society. All the people knew him in his neighborhood where he was on duty and he was always committed to fight social injustice.

He was a brave policeman and an employee in the secret service department.

He played a key role in searching for fugitives and investigating the failed murder attempt of Judge Falcone in Addaura in 1989.

On August 5, 1989, in the afternoon, Nino and Ida - with their baby in her womb - were going to Nino’s parents’ beach house to celebrate his sister’s birthday.

Nino, just 28, Ida, almost 20, and the never-born child were murdered by two killers.

The State funeral was attended by judges Falcone and Borsellino, along with the highest officers of the government.
His parents, Vincenzo and Augusta, are still waiting for the truth.
en.AgostinoGeofenceAlert: You are close to Villagrazia di Carini, here is where the policeman Antonino Agostino and his wife Ida Castelluccio were killed.
en.AparoDescription:
Filadelfo Aparo was an agent of the State Police and vice Brigadier Palermo's Squadra Mobile. He originally worked in the robbery section and then in the "Catturandi". He earned many awards and tributes due to the devotion and courage he put in his job.

He was almost certainly murdered by mafia clans for revenge; it is also believed that his murder occurred in order to eliminate a particularly efficient and dangerous "hound" (as he was called). Perhaps the murder occurred for both reasons: the sergeant was indeed investigating the structure of the mafia gangs in Palermo.

He was the brain of the Squadra Mobile, greatly admired by his colleagues and employees. He was a living archive of the "mafia clans" as he had discovered and memorized numerous faces over time.

He was murdered at the age of 43 in an ambush in Piazzale Tenente Anelli, on the morning of January 11, 1979. Aparo was shot with a "P 38" and a shotgun loaded with buckshot shortly after 8:30 AM. He was saying goodbye to his wife on the balcony of their home.
en.AparoGeofenceAlert: You are close to piazzale Tenente Giuseppe Anelli, here is where vice Brigadier Palermo's Squadra Mobile Filadelfo Aparo was killed.
en.BorsellinoBodyguardCatalanoDescription:
Agostino Catalano was born in Palermo on May 16, 1949. He was the assistant chief constable.

He married Maria Pace but on October 23, 1989 he became a widower. His wife died prematurely, leaving him with three children: Emanuele, Emilia and Rosalinda.

On the day of the Via D'Amelio massacre he was on vacation, but was called up to join Borsellino's protection team in order to make up the numbers. Usually Catalano was called upon to guard Father Bartolomeo Sorge.

One month before he died he saved a twelve-year old boy from drowning in the sea of Mondello.
en.BorsellinoBodyguardCosinaDescription:
Eddie Walter Cosina was born on July 25, 1961, in Norwood, Australia, to a family who were originally from Trieste but who had emigrated after the War.

At the age of 21 he lost his father and decided to enlist into the police. In 1983 he entered DIGOS (Italian Department of General Investigations and Special Operations) and from 1990 he was part of the anti-kidnapping team. Later he joined the Anti-Crime division.

After the Capaci massacre, the lack of bodyguards in Sicily increased their demand throughout Italy. Cosina agreed to move to Palermo.

He died six days before his 31st birthday.

He left behind his wife, Monica.
en.BorsellinoBodyguardLiMuliDescription:
Vincenzo Li Muli was born in Palermo on March 19, 1970. He had worked for the police for three years and was promoted to agent only a few months before the tragic event.

His sister said bitterly that deep inside, her brother was aware of what he was getting into, "A few days earlier he asked me to remind him how to recite The Lord's Prayer."

Agent Li Muli died at the age of 22, leaving his parents and siblings behind.
en.BorsellinoBodyguardLoiDescription:
Emanuela Loi was born in Sestu (Cagliari) on October 9, 1967.

After gaining a teaching diploma she enlisted into the Police Service in 1989 and attended the 119th course at the School for Agents in Trieste. She was passionate about her work, meticulous and scrupulous. She was also a sniper.

Two years later she moved to Palermo and joined judge Paolo Borsellino's police guard. Only one month later she would die.

She was the first female agent killed on duty. She died at the age of 24, leaving her parents, two siblings and her boyfriend behind.
en.BorsellinoBodyguardTrainaDescription:
Claudio Traina was born in Palermo on September 2, 1965.

After completing his military service in the Air Force he decided to join the police. He first attended the Police School in Alessandria, then he was transferred to Milan. Finally, at his request, he was moved to Palermo.

It was 1990 when Claudio decided to join the police protection team.

On the morning of July 19, he went fishing with his brother Luciano, who was also a police officer.

He left behind his wife and his eleven-month son, Dario.
en.BorsellinoDescription:
Paolo Borsellino was a magistrate: a magistrate who never turned his back.
He was born in Palermo on January 19, 1940, in Kalsa, a working class neighbourhood.
It was in Kalsa, when he was still a child, that he first met Giovanni Falcone. They would be friends forever.

He became a magistrate at the age of 22. In 1975, he entered the office of education of Palermo directed by Rocco Chinnici. Falcone was also there, and during this time they created an inseparable bond.
Along with other colleagues, they created an anti-mafia team that was to make the world aware of the mafia organization Cosa Nostra. With Falcone, he wrote the 8,000 page decree of the maxi trial of Palermo that sent 476 suspects to trial.
They would often joke, with cynicism and irony, about who would be killed first by the Cosa Nostra.

In the following years Paolo became chief Prosecutor in Marsala before returning to Palermo in the second half of 1991.

He was assassinated by the mafia on July 19, 1992 in via D'Amelio in Palermo. He was murdered 57 days after his friend Giovanni. His guards were wiped out as well.

One of the many reasons that the mafia decided to get rid of Borsellino was his intense dedication to seek the truth about the death of his best friend Giovanni Falcone.
en.BorsellinoGeofenceAlert: You are at 27 Via Mariano D’Amelio, where the magistrate Paolo Borsellino and his guards Agostino Catalano, Vincenzo Li Muli, Walter Eddie Cosina, Claudio Traina and Emanuela Loi were killed.
en.CassaraBodyguardAntiochiaDescription:
Roberto Antiochia was born in Terni on June 7, 1962.
After attending the Police school in Pescara he was first transferred to Turin, and then to Rome and Vicenza, then the Squadra Mobile of Palermo, to the section Catturandi directed by Dr. Beppe Montana. Engaged in delicate anti-mafia investigations along with Ninni Cassarà and his leader Montana, after the latter’s killing, despite being on vacation and already moved to Rome, he decided to stay in Palermo along with Cassarà to conduct the investigation on the murder of Beppe Montana.

On August 6, 1985 at 15:00 Antiochia and his colleague Natale Mondo, accompanied Ninni Cassara home, waiting for a fierce commander of the Cosa Nostra who met them with hundreds of bursts of Kalashnikov.

Cassara and Antiochia were killed, Mondo miraculously survived (he will later be killed in an ambush by the mafia on January 14, 1988).

His mother Saveria Antiochia (co-founder with Don Luigi Ciotti association Libera) honored the memory of his son and other victims of the mafia, while she lived.
Roberto Antiochia dies aged 23, leaving his parents, two brothers and girlfriend.
en.CassaraDescription:
Antonino Cassarà, also known as Ninni, was born in Palermo on May 7, 1947, a husband and a father of three children.

He was an officer of the State Police. He was special: one of those officers who in the evening placed his gun on the top shelf of the bookcase, "to keep it away from the children."

Ninni had introduced new working methods. He had successfully infiltrated his agents into the mafia organizations. One of these, agent Calogero Zucchetto, often made investigations on his Vespa in the streets of Palermo.

He believed that the best way to truly defeat the mafia was to educate the institutions about legality; this method would work especially for the younger generations. Indeed, Ninni loved to go to schools to talk to children.

Cassarà was a close associate of Judge Giovanni Falcone, and his investigations contributed to the statement of the first Maxi Trial.

He was killed (with agent of the Squadra Mobile Roberto Antiochia), outside his house, in Viale Croce Rossa, 81 on August 6, 1985. He died in the arms of his wife Laura. He was 37 years old.
en.CassaraGeofenceAlert: You are close to Viale Croce Rossa, here is where vice chief of the Palermo State Police Antonino "Ninni" Cassarà and agent of the Squadra Mobile Roberto Antiochia were killed.
en.ChinniciBodyguardBartolottaDescription:
Salvatore Bartolotta was born in Castrofilippo (AG) on 3rd March, 1935. Since his early childhood he wanted to join the Carabinieri Units. Once enlisted, he worked for a while in Caltanissetta and in Cefalù, and then he was assigned to Palermo’s Investigative Units at Carini military base.

In the late ‘70s he was charged with the delicate task of escorting Judge Rocco Chinnici; the task that cost him his life and the lives of sergeant Mario Trapassi, of Mr Stefano Li Sacchi and of the very Rocco Chinnici on 29th July, 1983, in Pipitone Federico Street, in Palermo.
en.ChinniciBodyguardLiSacchiDescription:
The story about Stefano Li Sacchi, born on 2nd June 1923, in Geraci Siculo (Palermo) is an absurd one. He was neither a police officer nor a carabiniere, it was not in his legal duty to face the danger, no.

He was a mere concierge of the building in Federico Pipitone Street in Palermo, where Judge Rocco Chinnici used to live. He was a kind and caring man, sincerely and disinterestedly devoted to Chinnici.

On the morning of 29th July, 1983, he was sweeping the entrance of the building in front of which the police officers Mario Trapassi and Salvatore Bartolotta were waiting for the judge. A car bomb erased the existence of all four of them throwing the body of the poor Li Sacchi tens of meters away from the explosion point.
en.ChinniciBodyguardTrapassiDescription:
Mario Trapassi was born in Palermo on 8th December, 1950. After enlisting into the Carabinieri Units, he attended the School for Non-commissioned Officers in Velletri and in Florence.

He was a serious and reliable police officer, always performing challenging assignments. After getting married he moved to Palermo where he asked and was accepted to join Paolo Borsellino’s escort team.

After the designation of Judge Rocco Chinnici as Chief Court Counselor in Palermo, Trapassi was given the delicate task of being in charge of Chinnici’s escort team. It was an extremely serious and delicate assignment and he carried it out conscientiously and with devotion.

This devotion cost him his life, and the lives of Corporal Salvatore Bartolotta, of Mr Stefano Li Sacchi and of Judge Rocco Chinnici, on the day of 29th July 1983.

It was the first car bomb attack on a judge.

He left a wife and four children behind.
en.ChinniciDescription:
Rocco Chinnici was born in Misilmeri (Pa) in 1925.
He was a judge, husband and father of three children.

In 1979 he created a turning point in the fight against mafia, he investigated the funds provided by the Region, he put in the spotlight the untouchable debt collector cousins, ​Nino and Ignazio Salvo and he reopened the case Impastato, about his death he said: "it is as if they have killed my son".
He was the judge who had the idea to set up the anti-mafia pool. Among the people who became part of his "team" there are some young magistrates, such as Giuseppe Di Lello, Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino.

He believed in the involvement of young people in the fight against the mafia.
He was the first magistrate to visit schools and tell students about the mafia and the danger of drugs.

He was killed with a car bomb – a green Fiat 126 comfortably parked overnight outside his home, in Federico Pipitone, 59 in Palermo, stuffed with 50 pounds of TNT.
It was on July 29, 1983 ... the only survivor Giovanni Paparcuri. "Palermo like Beirut" was the title on the newspapers.
en.ChinniciGeofenceAlert: You are at 59 of Via Giuseppe Pipitone Federico, here is where the judge Rocco Chinnici and his escort Mario Trapassi, Salvatore Bartolotta and the doorman building Stefano Li Sacchi​ were killed
en.CostaDescription:
Gaetano Costa was born in Caltanissetta, on March 1, 1916 and graduated from the Law School in Palermo. He won the Judiciary competition and enlisted as aviation official. After the war, he first worked in the Court of Rome and then in Caltanissetta where he became Magistrate, Deputy Prosecutor and Chief Prosecutor.

Since the sixties, he realized that the mafia had undergone a radical change. They were invading the centers of public administration and controlling procurement, recruitment and management. He helplessly drew the attention of the highest authorities to the fact that the fight against mafia demanded new legislative instruments that enabled the investigation of the mafia’s assets; it was the only way to hit them.

In January 1978, his appointment as chief prosecutor of Palermo was immediately obstructed because he did not begin working until the following July. He was immediately subjected to a tight control that forced him to a decisive clarification within the office itself. Costa began a series of delicate investigations attempting to penetrate the major assets of the mafia.
During one of these investigations, someone thought that placing him in a "minority" could stop him. However, it was not enough: he personally signed disputed arrest warrants. The disclosure of such facts was enough to trigger mafia’s revenge, as Sciascia will support after his death.

Due to these investigations, on August 6, 1980, Costa became a victim of the mafia, who murdered him in central Palermo. No one has been convicted for his death.

He was the only magistrate in Palermo who had been assigned an armored car and guard. He never took advantage of it because it would have put at risk those who had engaged in the same investigation. He did not want anyone to risk their life for him and he believed that the safety of a Magistrate is the certainty that, after his murder, the successor will continue to work on his path.
en.CostaGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Cavour, here is where chief prosecutor of Palermo Gaetano Costa was killed.
en.DallaChiesaBodyguardRussoDescription:
Domenico Russo was born in Santa Maria Capua Vetere (CE) December 27, 1950.

He was a Police Officer and was given the task of being a personal guard to General Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa in those 100 days when he was Prefect of Palermo.

On the evening of September 3, 1982 he headed the service Alfetta that followed the A112 driven by Prefect Dalla Chiesa who was with his wife Emanuela Setti Carraro as was often his habit.

In Via Isidoro Carini, Palermo, the A112 of the General was flanked by two killers who shot bursts of Kalashnikov at Dalla Chiesa and his young wife.

Russo was approched by another killer who let off multiple gunshot wounds that seriously wounded him. He tried to react but without success.

He died on 15 September after a long agony.

He leaves a wife and two young children.

He was recognized as the Gold Medal for Civil Valour.
en.DallaChiesaDescription:
Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa was born in Saluzzo (Piemonte) on September 27, 1920.

In 1942, after fighting in Montenegro, he enrolled in the Carabinieri – the Italian police. He became head of the Lieutenancy of San Benedetto del Tronto, where he joined the partisan bands in the Resistance. In 1945, he married Dora Fabbo, whom he met in Bari as a child. They had three children together.

Later he worked in Casoria, Florence, Corleone, Como, Milan, Rome, Turin, Milan once again and then Palermo, where he served the country from 1966 to 1973.

In 1973, he became commander of the Northwest Military Region and created "the special anti - terrorist unit ", through which he achieved great successes in the fight against the Red Brigades.

In February of 1978, Dalla Chiesa lost his wife Dora in a very dramatic experience. In August 1978, after the kidnapping and murder of Aldo Moro, Dalla Chiesa became the leader of the fight against terrorism throughout the country.

On December 16, 1981 he was promoted to Vice Commander of the Army; in March 1982, he was appointed Prefect of Palermo where he was urgently sent on the day that Pio La Torre was murdered (April 30, 1982). The goal was to get the same brilliant results, obtained against the Red Brigades, in the fight against Cosa Nostra. Dalla Chiesa accepted his new position but clarified that only special powers could the success of such mission.

Obviously this never happened, and only one hundred days after his arrival in Palermo, on September 3, 1982, Dalla Chiesa was murdered. The murder occurred in the evening, while he was driving an A112 accompanied by his young wife Emanuela Setti Carraro and escorted by the driver Domenico Russo. A BMW got beside him and shot hundreds of bullets that killed him and his wife instantly. At the same time, a man on a motorcycle killed agent Russo.

Immediately after these brutal murders, that have upset the public opinion, someone left a sign at the place of murder with the following inscription "the hope of the honest people of Palermo died here".
en.DallaChiesaGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Isidoro Carini,  here is where General Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa was killed.
en.DeMauroDescription:
Mauro De Mauro was born in Foggia in 1921.
He was a journalist for L’Ora newspaper. Precise and punctual at work, he was known for his investigations that irritated the mafia.

On the evening of September 16, 1970, his daughter Franca Valeria and her boyfriend met him while he was getting out of his car, parked just outside his house at 58, Viale delle Magnolie.

However, right after this the couple saw him leaving with some people in the car.
Since that day, De Mauro disappeared forever. His body was never found. Based on the most reliable reconstructions, De Mauro was strangled the same night of the kidnapping in a farm in Santa Maria di Gesu’. The corpse was walled in along the highway or at the mouth of the river Oreto, and perhaps it was later exhumed and dissolved in acid so that no traces would remain.

The written judgment stipulates, however, that De Mauro "died because he had gone too far in his search for the truth about the Mattei case in Sicily" and that he died in a mysterious plane crash.
en.DeMauroGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via delle Magnolie, here the the journalist Mauro De Mauro disappeared
en.FalconeBodyguardDicilloDescription:
Rocco Dicillo was born in Triggiano (Bari) on 13th April, 1962.

Having passed the entrance exam for the Police, he left the University. In 1989 he was assigned to the Security Department of Palermo’s Police Headquarters as one of the police officers of Giovanni Falcone’s escort team.

On the afternoon of 23th May, 1992, while he and his colleagues were accompanying the Judge Falcone and his wife Francesca Morvillo home, Rocco was sitting on the back seat of the leading motorcade car, together with Antonino Montinaro and Vito Schifani. Their armoured vehicle was blown up by the TNT set by the mafia in the tunnel of the A29 highway, near Capaci exit.

He and other police officers died on impact, the car was hurled in an orchard nearby.

Rocco Dicillo was buried in a Triggiano cemetery, in his home town, where a square and a street were named after him. He left his parents, three sisters and his girlfriend behind.
en.FalconeBodyguardMontinaroDescription:
Antonio Montinaro was born in Calimera (Lecce) on 8th September, 1962. He worked for the Police Escort Department of Palermo’s Headquarters and was in charge of the Judge Giovanni Falcone’s escort team. He was absolutely aware of the risky task he had to cope with, but he carried it out without hesitation.

He was in the first car of the motorcade escorting the judge, with Vito Schifani as a driver and agent Rocco Dicillo on the back seat.

Near the Capaci exit of the A29 highway a bomb exploded beneath them killing the three police officers on the spot.

He was married with Tina Martinez with whom he had two children: Giovanni and Gaetano.

The District of Calimera named a square after him as memorial and set up a small monument made of a boulder pulled out from the place of the attack and of a Sicilian mandarin tree.
en.FalconeBodyguardMorvilloDescription:
Francesca Morvillo was born in Palermo, on 14th December, 1945. She graduated in Law at the University of Palermo when she was only 22 years old.

Keeping the family tradition and following the footsteps of her father Guido, Deputy Prosecutor in Palermo, and of her brother Alfredo, she decided to join the judiciary.

In 1968 she passed brilliantly the public examination for Auditor Judge.

Her career initially included practicing as a Judge in the Court of Agrigento, as Deputy Public Prosecutor at the Juvenile Court of Palermo, as Director of Appeal of Palermo and as a member of the Commission for Competitive Entry into the magistracy.

She was killed in the Capaci Massacre, as well as her husband Giovanni Falcone and three members of a police escort, on 23rd May, 1992.
en.FalconeBodyguardSchifaniDescription:
Vito Schifani was born in Palermo on 23rd February, 1965. On 23rd May, 1992, he was in a brown Fiat Croma escorting the magistrate Giovanni Falcone and his wife Francesca Morvillo, right behind him in their white Croma, from Palermo's Punta Raisi airport.

Vito was driving with Antonio Montinaro, in charge of the police escort team, seated next to him, and with Rocco Dicillo on the back seat.

Their car, the first one in the motorcade, was hit hard by the TNT explosive planted in the tunnel of the A29 highway, near Capaci exit, and Vito and his colleagues had no chances to survive.

Vito was an athlete specialized in the 400 meters and would have run a race on the evening of 23rd May 1992. The Palermo’s Stadium of Palms was named after him.

Vito Schifani’s big dream would have come true: he wanted to become a police helicopter pilot, and few months later he would have started his training lessons, but his dream touched down even before it took off.

He was married with Rosaria Costa, 22 years old at the moment of his death, and a newborn son, Emanuele Schifani, today a police officer.
en.FalconeDescription:
Giovanni Falcone was born in Palermo on May 18, 1939. Since 1978, under the guidance of Rocco Chinnici and together with his close friend Paolo Borsellino, he worked on more than 500 cases against Cosa Nostra.

His work continued after Chinnici’s death, with Antonino Caponnetto as an investigating judge. The turning point came in 1984 when, thanks to Tommaso Buscetta - an informant - the Maxi Trial was held and resulted in 360 convictions.

In 1989 the mafia tried to take revenge by placing a bag in the Falcone's villa in Palermo with fifty-eight sticks of dynamite on a cliff where the magistrate used to swim in his spare time. This was one of the few moments of relaxation he allowed himself.

In the early ’90s Falcone faced strong criticism. The hostile atmosphere at Palermo’s Court of Justice was increasing day by day and the magistrate soon realized he remained alone in his battle.

In the 1991 he worked as Director of the Department of Criminal Affairs of the Ministry of Justice providing the basis for laws for future legal processes.

The following year, the historic sentence of the Supreme Court confirmed the verdicts of the Palermo’s Maxi Trial. This was his victory and yet also his death sentence.

On May 23, 1992, Giovanni and his wife Francesca Morvillo, on their way back from Rome, landed at Palermo Airport, where three "Quarto Savona 15" cars, with a close-knit police squad inside, were waiting for them.

After exiting the airport, just after taking the highway, near the exit for Capaci, at 17:58, a half-ton of explosives detonated, blowing the cars up. Falcone was killed, as well as his wife Francesca Morvillo and all three members of his police protection unit: Vito Schifani, Rocco Dicillo and Antonio Montinaro ... the only survivor Giuseppe Costanza.
en.FalconeGeofenceAlert: You are near Capaci, here is where the judge Giovanni Falcone, his wife Francesca Morvillo and his escort Vito Schifani, Rocco Dicillo, Antonio Montinaro​were killed.
en.FranceseDescription:
Mario Francese was born on February 6, 1925 in Syracuse.
He was a journalist for the Giornale di Sicilia who was always in search of knowing about the good and bad public figures.

He tried to analyze the mafia organizations. He was a true news hunter.
He was the first to name Riina and the only one to interview Riina's girlfriend, Antonietta Bagarella.
He wrote the ascent of the Corleone family, their strategy of terror, their allies, their contracts, in particular the trafficking billion for the construction of the Garcia dam, after the earthquake in 1968.

On the evening of January 26, 1979, after saying goodbye to colleagues with the usual farewell, "Men of Colorado, I salute you and go!" he went downstairs. He was immediately killed by six shots fired by Leoluca Bagarella.
en.FranceseGeofenceAlert: You are at 15 of Viale Campania, here is where the journalist Mario Francese was killed
en.GiacconeDescription:
Paolo Giaccone was one of the greatest experts in forensics in Italy.
He was professor of forensic medicine for the Faculty of Law and the whole campus of Palermo.

He had developed an investigative technique that has been adopted by the FBI as well. He was also founder of the section of AVIS in Palermo.
He did the reports and autopsies on famous people killed by the mafia, such as the President of the Sicilian Region Piersanti Mattarella, prosecutor Gaetano Costa, judge Cesare Terranova, and journalist Mario Francese.

In December 1981, following a shooting among some mafia clans in the streets of Bagheria, Giaccone was commissioned to examine Giuseppe Marchese’s fingerprint. He was the grandson of the “Corso dei Mille” mafia boss Filippo Marchese and his fingerprint was the only evidence that could trap the killer. The doctor was pressured to change the results of the fingerprint. Giaccone did not change anything despite the repeated threats.

On the morning of August 11, 1982, shortly after eight o'clock, as Giaccone was walking to the hospital Policlinico di Palermo, he was shot and killed by two killers. He was 53 years old and left a wife and four children.
en.GiacconeGeofenceAlert: You are close to Policlinico, here is where the doctor Paolo Giaccone was killed.
en.GiulianoDescription:
Giorgio Boris Giuliano was a police officer, loved by his agents, deeply respected by ordinary people, feared by the corrupt and considered the number one enemy of Cosa Nostra.
He was born in Piazza Armerina, on October 22, 1930.
He was a husband and father of three children and entered the police force in 1962. After the massacre of Ciaculli, which cost the lives of five policemen and two soldiers from the army, Giuliano asked to be transferred to Palermo.

He was the first Italian to attend the FBI Academy in Quantico. He became head of the Squadra Mobile in 1976: he worked on all of the most heinous crimes that bloodied the city of Palermo, from the massacre of Viale Lazio, to the De Mauro crime.

He was the first to understand that at that time Sicily had a crucial role in the international trafficking of drugs.
Due to his deep knowledge of the mafia and the dynamics of the gangs, he was a terrible threat to the mafia.

On July 8, 1979, Giuliano and his men found Leoluca Bagarella's hideout. He was a member of the Corleone clan who was on the run.

Thirteen days later, while he was getting a coffee in a bar, he was killed by seven gunshots from behind. The killer was Leoluca Bagarella.
en.GiulianoGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Francesco Paolo Di Blasi, where the Deputy Commissioner Boris Giuliano was killed.
en.GrassiDescription:
Libero Grassi was born in Catania in 1924. At the age of 8 he and his family moved to Palermo. Anti-Fascist, after graduating in Law, he gave up his dream of undertaking a diplomatic career to start his own business in the textile industry.
Together with his wife Pina Maisano, he began running an historic textile store in Palermo city center.

Libero and Pina had two children, a boat and flourishing business.
Everything seemed to be going well until one day Cosa Nostra picked on the historic "Sigma" factory, asking for blackmail money.

Grassi, unlike other businessmen, had the courage to oppose the racket requests and to speak out by denouncing the extortionists, with even his employees helping him by revealing the identity of some of them.

Grassi’s death sentence arrived after the publication of a letter in the Giornale di Sicilia in which he refused to give in to the mafia’s blackmailing.
Left all alone in this fight by his fellow businessmen and institutions, he was killed on August 29, 1991.

Two men armed with 38 - caliber pistols fired four gunshots leaving him in a pool of blood.
On that terrible day he was going to work, as usual, in the city in which he wanted to live and feel, just like his name said: free.
en.GrassiGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Vittorio Alfieri, here is where the entrepreneur Libero Grassi was killed.
en.IanniDescription:
Carmelo Iannì was born in Palermo on February 26, 1934.
He was a hotel entrepreneur, who was married with three daughters.

In 1977 he took over a small hotel in Carini, near Palermo, located right on the seafront, the "Riva Smeralda".
He was passionate about taking care of tourists, welcoming them and pampering them while making them feel at home.

The turning point in Carmelo’s life came in 1980, when the police asked him to allow undercover agents in his hotel to expose some criminals from Marseilles, who were in Sicily to teach the mafia how to refine heroin. Carmelo immediately said "yes".

For nearly a month, during the investigation, the police intercepted phone conversations, until the day of the raid of a house in Trabia, near Palermo.

Among those arrested, was also the fugitive Gerlando Alberti.
Straight after the raid, the mafia boss - from prison - ordered Carmelo Iannì’s murder, as he was responsible for helping the police with the investigation.

Four days after his arrest, a commando of two people broke into the hotel lobby and shot Carmelo Iannì, killing him instantly, in front of his wife.
The murder happened on August 28, 1980.

The journalist Saverio Lodato identified Iannì as "the first civilian victim of the mafia", while Carlo Lucarelli called him "a normal hero".
en.IanniGeofenceAlert: You are close to Villagrazia di Carini, here is where the entrepreneur Carmelo Iannì was killed.
en.ImpastatoDescription:
Peppino Impastato was born to a mafia family. Peppino’s father Luigi, despite not having a leading role, was very close to his brother-in-law Cesare Manzella, the village’s mafia boss, who died in 1963 in the first car bomb attack.

Right from the beginning, Peppino’s choices were so opposing to those of his birth environment that his father kicked him out of the house. In 1965, he founded the newspaper "L’Idea socialista" and adhered to PSIUP (wing of the socialist party hostile to the alliance with the Christian Democrats).

In 1976, he founded Radio Aut, a self-financed free radio, through which he denounced the crimes and dealings of the mafia in Cinisi and Terrasini. The most followed radio program was "onda pazza", a satirical broadcast about mafia and politics. Costa created the term "Mafiopoli", spread names and surnames of politicians, and put to shame the mafia boss Gaetano Badalamenti (often called "Tano Seduto").

In 1978, he was a candidate for the municipal elections in the Proletarian Democracy category. However, he was murdered in the night between May 8 and 9, 1978, during the election campaign. A charge of dynamite was placed under his body tied on the railroad tracks: many assumed it was suicide or he died while organizing an attack.

Twenty years after his death, the investigations on Peppino’s death were reopened, thanks to the efforts of his mother Felicia Bartolotta (died on December 7, 2004), his brother Giovanni, several political activists, and the "Sicilian Documentation Centre" (opened in 1977 and named after Peppino). The investigations demonstrated that he was kidnapped and killed before being laid on the tracks with a bomb.

In 2001, the mafia boss Vito Palazzolo was convicted for Peppino’s murder and sentenced to thirty years in prison. In 2002, Gaetano Badalamenti was indeed sentenced to life imprisonment.
en.ImpastatoGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via 9 maggio 1978, nearby Giuseppe "Peppino" Impastato was killed.
en.LaTorreBodyguardDiSalvoDescription:
Rosario di Salvo was born in Bari, on 16th August, 1946. He married Rosa Canova in Palermo and emigrated to Germany.

Few years later he came back to Sicily, enrolled in the Italian Communist Party and shortly after became one of the most active and appreciated militants of ICP’s Secretariat. He established a strong bond with Achille Occhetto, who was a Regional Secretary back then.

As soon as he met Pio La Torre he became his right-hand man and his personal driver. Di Salvo was a courageous and determined person with quick reflexes. When on 30th April, 1982, a car, in which Di Salvo and La Torre were, was flanked by a motorcycle from which the killers fired dozens of gunshots, Di Salvo had strength to react quickly and shot five bullets, without hitting the bullseye though.

During his funeral, Enrico Berlinguer, in front of a hundred thousand people, praised his courageousness and loyalty to his ideals.
en.LaTorreDescription:
Pio La Torre was born in Palermo on December 24, 1927 from a family of poor farm laborers. When he was a teenager, in a period of peasant struggles, he joined the Italian Communist Party.

During these events he faced the shame of prison when he was arrested in 1950; he was brought to the Ucciardone and was falsely accused of assault during the occupation of a feud in Bisacquino. After 17 months, he was acquitted and released.

A new political career that led La Torre to become a national deputy had begun. As a parliamentarian, in 1976, he drew up the report of the Anti-Mafia Commission, which accused Giovanni Gioia, Vito Ciancimino and Salvo Lima to have connections with the mafia.

In 1980, he prepared the Rognoni-La Torre innovative law, which introduced the crime of "association with the mafia" into the Penal Code and the subsequent confiscation of assets from criminal organizations. This law, however, was only approved after his death along with that of General Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa, in September 1982.

La Torre, who was a close associate of Enrico Berlinguer, became secretary of the Sicilian Communist Party in 1981. At this point, he organized an historic march against the construction of the military base in Comiso and contributed to the largest peace movement in European history.

The mafia killed La Torre in Palermo on April 30, 1982, along with Rosario Di Salvo. More than 100,000 people attended his funeral.
en.LaTorreGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Vincenzo Li Muli (ex Via Generale Turba), here is where Pio La Torre and Rosario Di Salvo were killed.
en.MattarellaDescription:
Piersanti Mattarella was born in Castellammare del Golfo, on May 24, 1935.
He was a Christian Democrat statesman, close to Aldo Moro, who created a turning point in the regional administration.

When he was President of the Sicilian government he broadened the political majority, involving the communist party in the administration. He did so in order to push forward his reform plan, regenerating the inner life of his party and dismantling the dark power games found in the public administration.

The commitment to the rule of law and the development of the south inspired all of his administrative and political activities.

He died on the day of the Epiphany in 1980, murdered by a killer while he was inside his car, in front of his family. All of them were about to go to mass.

The first to arrive at the scene of the murder, his brother Sergio, the current president of the Italian Republic, tried to help him. Piersanti died in his arms.
en.MattarellaGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Libertà, here is where the ex Sicily Region President Piersanti Mattarella was killed.
en.MontanaDescription:
Beppe Montana was born in Agrigento on October 8, 1951. After graduating in law, he won a competition to get into the State Police. When he was 30, he moved to Palermo, just a few days after the murder of General Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa.

In Palermo, while working in the investigation section of the Squadra Mobile, he found himself alongside Ninni Cassarà. Together they created the "Report of the 162", which was the first document to map the Cosa Nostra clans. The report showed the close ties between boss Michele Greco and others from the mafia. This document was considered by Giovanni Falcone as "essential to pursue the Maxi Trial".

Beppe Montana was a modern, stubborn and tireless investigator who always worked around the clock. Unwilling to sit behind his desk, his colleagues nicknamed him "Serpico" because he preferred moving around the streets and neighborhoods of the city, like American policemen do in movies.

His intuition brought to life the Catturandi Squad that specialized in researching the great fugitives.
Montana was able to arrest several wanted criminals. He also discovered a very large number of arsenals of weapons and drug refineries managed by the mafia.

Beppe Montana was killed on July 28, 1985, when he was only 34. He was murdered after spending a day at the beach with his friends and girlfriend. A few days later, Cosa Nostra killed his friends and colleagues Ninni Cassarà and Roberto Antiochia as well. They never saw the beginning of the Maxi process.
en.MontanaGeofenceAlert: You are close to the Porticello dock, here is where the police commissioner Giuseppe Montana was killed.
en.PuglisiDescription:
Giuseppe Puglisi (known as Pino) was born in Palermo in the Brancaccio neighborhood on September 15, 1937.
In 1953, he entered the Diocesan seminary in Palermo and on July 2, 1960 he was ordained a priest. His evangelical responsibility occurred in the most marginalized neighborhoods of the city of Palermo (Settecannoli, Brancaccio) where he closely followed the problems of young people with social difficulties.

At an early age Father Pino taught in many Sicilian schools; he taught both math at the juvenile Seminary and religion in public schools. Such educational activity lasted for thirty years, until the day of his death.
He was made parson of the church of St. Gaetano in Brancaccio on September 29, 1990. Brancaccio was a mafia-controlled neighborhood. The Gravano brothers were the main leaders, and were also related to boss Leoluca Bagarella.
In Brancaccio, Father Pino began taking care of the teenagers to avoid their recruitment by the mafia.

His unceasing efforts to help young people took dozens of teens and children off the street, who otherwise would have become involved in criminal activities. However, such activity caused the hostility of the mafia bosses who saw Father Pino as an obstacle to be eliminated.

On January 29, 1993, Father Pino opened the Padre Nostro center in Brancaccio, for human promotion and evangelization.
After several threats and a lot of intimidation, on September 15, 1993 (the day of his 56th birthday), Father Pino was killed in front of his house.

Father Pino Puglisi, was beatified on May 25, 2013 in Palermo in front of one hundred thousand faithful.
en.ScaglioneBodyguardLoRussoDescription:
Antonino Lorusso was born in Ruvo di Puglia (Bari) in 1929. He was a correctional officer at Ucciardone prison, but it had been a while since he started working as a driver of Pietro Scaglione, a Chief Prosecutor in the Court of Palermo.

His life, along with the Judge Scaglione’s one, was horrible lost on the morning of 5th May, 1971, while, shortly after they had left the cemetery of Cappuccini in Palermo, he was taking the Prosecutor to the Court.

One of the first people to arrive at the crime scene, by pure coincidence, and to recognize the body, was his own brother Mario Lorusso, a carabiniere, who was taking the Commanding General to the murder scene, without knowing that one of the victims was actually his brother Antonino.
en.ScaglioneDescription:
Pietro Scaglione was born in Lercara Friddi, on March 2, 1906.
In 1928 he enrolled in judiciary. He was one of the first judges who devoted himself with passion and determination to fight against the mafia and corruption.

He was defined as a "ruthless mafia persecutor" and investigated serious criminal acts, including the mysterious Gaspare Pisciotta murder in prison, the mafia massacre in Ciaculli, and the journalist Mauro De Mauro's disappearance. He also investigated the mafia-politics connections.

He was killed during a mafia ambush on May 5, 1971, in Via Cipressi in Palermo, along with agent Lorusso. A few minutes earlier he had prayed at the grave of his wife, Concettina Abate.
Pietro Scaglione was the first judge killed by the mafia.
en.ScaglioneGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Cipressi, here is where the Public Prosecutor Pietro Scaglione and the police officer Antonio Lorusso​were killed.
en.TerranovaBodyguardMancusoDescription:
Lenin Mancuso was a Marshal of the Security Services, he was born on 6th November, 1929, in Rota Greta in the province of Cosenza; his father, convinced Bolshevik and anti-Fascist, chose to call him "Lenin" as an act of defiance of Mussolini, a cumbersome name that caused him some problems to enter the Security Services.

He was a friend, right-hand man and a member of the magistrate Cesare Terranova’s escort team for more than twenty years. On the morning of 25th September, 1979, Lenin Mancuso went to pick up the Judge. Terranova began driving, and few meters later both of them were caught in a mafia ambush. Lenin only had time to throw himself on Terranova’s body to shield him, but his courageous act of sacrifice was useless.
en.TerranovaDescription:
Cesare Terranova was born in Petralia Soprana in 1921.
He was a brave and determined judge. He was married with no children.

Terranova sensed the potential danger that the mafia was developing. In 1974 he managed to prosecute and sentence to life Luciano Leggio, Corleone's "Primula rossa". This prosecution was the first great victory of the State against the mafia. The boss did not forget.

He was deputy to the National Chamber, from the PCI list as independent leftist. He worked closely with Pio La Torre. In 1979 he decided to wear his gown again and continue his work.

He was killed on September 25, of the same year in Palermo. He was murdered near his house while he was driving a Fiat 131. At his side there was the trusted marshal Lenin Mancuso, his guard for twenty years (just like an angel for Terranova) who was killed as well.

Terranova's neighbors in the building under which he was killed did not allow a plaque to be put in place to remember the incident.

en.ZucchettoDescription:
Calogero Zucchetto, called Lillo among friends, was born in Sutera on February 3, 1955.

He was a policeman, a real one, one of those who loved the roads, investigating people, and stalking criminals. He was a man with value and great courage.

He joined the Police when he was very young, starting his apprenticeship when he was 19, in Judge Falcone's first rudimentary escort. In the early 80s, he joined Palermo's Squadra Mobile, headed by Ninni Cassarà.

He used to go around on his "Vespone" (even when he was out of duty and paying the gasoline out of his pocket) to seek out and spy on Cosa Nostra's soldiers. He searched in areas where the bosses felt the most protected.

On November 14, 1982, two months after General Dalla Chiesa was murdered, two ruthless killers waited for Zucchetto outside the Collica Bar, in the center of Palermo, in via Notarbartolo. It was Sunday evening, 9:30 pm. They shot five bullets in his head with a .38 and escaped on a motorcycle. Calogero Zucchetto was 27 years old and he would have married a few months later.
en.ZucchettoGeofenceAlert: You are close to Via Notarbartolo, here is where the policeman Calogero Zucchetto was killed.

it.AgostinoDescription:
Antonino Agostino, detto Nino, nasce a Palermo il 29 marzo del 1961. Sposato con Ida Castelluccio e in attesa del primo figlio, era un agente del commissariato San Lorenzo.

Un ragazzo vivace e leale che lottava per una società più giusta. Era conosciuto da tutti gli abitanti del quartiere in cui era in servizio per il suo continuo impegno contro le ingiustizie sociali.

Poliziotto coraggioso e collaboratore dei servizi segreti ha avuto un ruolo fondamentale nella ricerca dei latitanti e nelle indagini del fallito attentato al giudice Falcone all'Addaura del 21 giugno 1989.

Era il pomeriggio del 5 Agosto del 1989, Nino e Ida, con in grembo il loro bambino, stavano raggiungendo la casa al mare dei genitori di Nino per festeggiare il compleanno della sorella.

Furono uccisi da due killer: Nino di soli 28 anni, Ida quasi 20 e il bambino mai nato.

Ai funerali di stato erano presenti i giudici Falcone e Borsellino e le più alte cariche dello stato.

I suoi genitori, Vincenzo e Augusta, aspettano ancora la verità.
it.AgostinoGeofenceAlert: Sei in prossimità di Villagrazia di Carini, qua è avvenuto l’attentato al poliziotto Antonino Agostino e alla moglie Ida Castelluccio.

it.AparoDescription:
Era un agente della Polizia di Stato, vice Brigadiere della Squadra Mobile di Palermo, in servizio prima alla sezione antirapina e poi alla "Catturandi". Per il suo coraggio e la dedizione al dovere meritò numerosi premi e riconoscimenti.

Il suo assassinio si deve quasi certamente alla vendetta delle cosche, o alla decisione di eliminare un "segugio" (come veniva chiamato) particolarmente efficiente e pericoloso o, probabilmente, per entrambi i motivi: il sottufficiale era infatti impegnato in delicate indagini per scoprire la struttura delle cosche mafiose palermitane.

Era il cervello fotografico della Squadra Mobile, il più ascoltato dai colleghi e funzionari, un archivio vivente della "mala".

Fu assassinato a 43 anni in un agguato in Piazzale Tenente Anelli, la mattina dell’11 gennaio 1979, poco dopo le 8:30 con numerosi colpi di una "P 38" e un fucile a canne mozze caricato a pallettoni di lupara, mentre salutava la moglie affacciata al balcone di casa.
it.AparoGeofenceAlert: Sei in prossimità di piazzale Tenente Giuseppe Anelli, qua è avvenuto l’attentato al vice Brigadiere della Squadra mobile di Palermo Filadelfo Aparo.

it.BorsellinoBodyguardCatalanoDescription:
Agostino Catalano nasce a Palermo il 16 maggio 1949. Ha la qualifica di Assistente Capo della Polizia di Stato.

La sua famiglia era stata già colpita da un grave lutto: il 23 ottobre del 1989, purtroppo, rimase vedovo. La moglie Maria Pace era morta prematuramente lasciandolo con tre ragazzi: Emanuele, Emilia e Rosalinda.

Anche lui muore prematuramente e "per caso": fu per caso, infatti, che il giorno della Strage di Via D'Amelio fosse il Capo Scorta di Borsellino. Solitamente Catalano era assegnato alla scorta di padre Bartolomeo Sorge; era in ferie, ma fu chiamato a svolgere quel servizio, per raggiungere un numero sufficiente di operatori, e lui non disse di no...

Un mese prima di morire aveva salvato un dodicenne che stava annegando nel mare di Mondello.
it.BorsellinoBodyguardCosinaDescription:
Eddie Walter Cosina nasce il 25 luglio 1961 a Norwood, in Australia, da una famiglia di origine triestina emigrata nel dopoguerra.

Dopo la morte del padre, quando lui aveva ventuno anni, decide di entrare nella Polizia di Stato. Nel 1983 viene assegnato alla Digos ed a partire dal 1990 fa parte del Nucleo Anti Sequestri. In seguito, prende servizio presso la Divisione Anticrimine.

Gli piaceva il "servizio attivo" e, infatti, dopo la strage di Capaci, in considerazione dell’emergenza e dell’urgenza di nuovo personale, accetta di far parte del reparto Scorte della Questura di Palermo e viene trasferito.

Muore a soli sei giorni dal suo trentunesimo compleanno.
Lascia la moglie Monica.
it.BorsellinoBodyguardLiMuliDescription:
La vicenda di Vincenzo Li Muli, il più giovane della pattuglia, ci fa capire quanto possa essere importante, in momenti di "crisi", sapere a memoria cose semplici...

Vincenzo Li Muli nasce a Palermo il 19 marzo 1970. Da tre anni nella Polizia di Stato, aveva ottenuto pochi mesi prima la nomina ad agente effettivo.

La sorella racconta con amarezza la consapevolezza del fratello che, in fondo, sapeva bene a cosa stava andando incontro: «Qualche sera prima mi chiese di ricordargli come si recitava il Padre Nostro» - dice.

Cosa c’è di più semplice e immediato di un Padre Nostro?

L’Agente Li Muli muore a 22 anni, lasciando i genitori ed i fratelli.
it.BorsellinoBodyguardLoiDescription:
Emanuela Loi nasce a Sestu (Cagliari) il 9 ottobre 1967.

Emanuela si era diplomata al Liceo Magistrale, ma ad una "sicura" cattedra, preferisce lo scomodo sedile di una Volante.

Decide, infatti, di arruolarsi nella Polizia di Stato e nel 1989 frequenta il 119º corso di Formazione per Agenti presso la Scuola Allievi di Trieste. Appassionata del suo lavoro, pignola e scrupolosa, era anche una formidabile tiratrice.

Trasferita a Palermo due anni dopo, entra nella scorta del giudice Paolo Borsellino, solo un mese prima di morire.

Raccontano i colleghi che era molto contenta del suo nuovo incarico.

È stata la prima agente donna ad essere uccisa in servizio. Muore a 24 anni, lasciando i genitori, due fratelli ed il fidanzato.
it.BorsellinoBodyguardTrainaDescription:
Si è portati a pensare che fare cose normali, forse pure banali, poco prima di un impegno particolare, in qualche modo possa metterti al riparo da "eventi eccezionali". Ma non è così, purtroppo.

Claudio Traina nasce a Palermo il 2 settembre 1965. Dopo avere svolto il servizio militare nell’ aeronautica, decide di entrare in Polizia.Prima frequenta la scuola di Polizia ad Alessandria, poi viene trasferito alle Volanti a Milano.Infine il trasferimento, come da sua richiesta, a Palermo.

E’ il 1990 e Claudio decide di farsi assegnare all’ ufficio scorte.

La mattina del 19 luglio era andato a pesca con il fratello Luciano, anch’ egli poliziotto, per trascorrere un paio d’ ore di banale relax.

Lascia la moglie ed un figlio, Dario di undici mesi.
it.BorsellinoDescription:
Paolo Borsellino è stato un magistrato, di quelli che non si tiravano mai indietro. Nato a Palermo il 19 gennaio 1940, nel quartiere popolare della Kalsa, è qui che da bambino conosce Giovanni Falcone, quello che sarà il suo amico per sempre. Diventa magistrato a 22 anni.

Nel 1975 entra nell’ufficio istruzione diretto da Rocco Chinnici, dove trova anche Falcone creando così un binomio inscindibile.

Entra a far parte del pool antimafia che farà conoscere al mondo l’organizzazione Cosa nostra.

Con Falcone scrive l’ordinanza di 8 mila pagine del maxiprocesso di Palermo che rinviava a giudizio 476 indagati.

Spesso, con spirito cinico ed ironico, scherzavano su chi fra i due sarebbe morto per primo per mano di Cosa Nostra.

Negli anni successivi Paolo fu procuratore capo a Marsala, per poi tornare a lavorare a Palermo nella seconda metà del 1991.

Muore per mano della mafia il 19 luglio 1992 in via D’Amelio a Palermo, 57 giorni dopo l’amico Giovanni. Con lui fu annientata la sua scorta, composta da Agostino Catalano, Vincenzo Li Muli, Walter Eddie Cosina, Claudio Traina ed Emanuela Loi.

Tra i tanti motivi per cui la mafia decise di farlo fuori, anche il suo intenso impegno nel cercare la verità sulla morte dell’amico perduto Giovanni.
it.BorsellinoGeofenceAlert: Sei in prossimità di via Mariano d’Amelio 27, qua è avvenuto l’attentato al magistrato Paolo Borsellino con la sua scorta: Agostino Catalano, Vincenzo Li Muli, Walter Eddie Cosina, Claudio Traina ed Emanuela Loi.

it.CassaraBodyguardAntiochiaDescription:
Roberto Antiochia nasce a Terni il 7 giugno 1962.
Dopo aver frequentato la scuola di Polizia a Pescara viene trasferito prima a Torino, poi a Roma e Vicenza, quindi alla Squadra Mobile di Palermo, alla sezione Catturandi diretta dal Dr. Beppe Montana. Impegnato in delicate indagini antimafia insieme a Ninni Cassarà e al suo capo Montana, dopo l’uccisione di quest’ultimo, pur essendo in ferie e già trasferito a Roma, decise di restare a Palermo per condurre insieme a Cassarà le indagini sull’omicidio di Beppe Montana.

Alle ore 15:00 del 6 agosto 1985 Antiochia e il collega Natale Mondo, accompagnarono a casa Ninni Cassarà, ad attenderli un feroce commando di Cosa Nostra che li accolse con centinaia di raffiche di kalashnikov.

Cassarà e Antiochia furono uccisi, Mondo si salvò miracolosamente (sarà successivamente ucciso in un agguato mafioso il 14 gennaio 1988).

La madre Saveria Antiochia (cofondatrice insieme a Don Luigi Ciotti dell’Associazione Libera) finché ha vissuto, ha onorato la memoria del figlio e delle altre vittime di mafia.
Roberto Antiochia muore a 23 anni, lasciando i genitori, due fratelli e la fidanzata.
it.CassaraDescription:
Antonino Cassarà, detto Ninni, nasce a Palermo il 7 maggio 1947. Sposato e padre di tre figli.
Era vice questore di Palermo. Un poliziotto speciale, di quelli che la sera posava la pistola sullo scaffale più alto della libreria, "per non farla vedere ai bambini".

Ninni aveva ideato nuovi metodi lavorativi, introducendo poliziotti infiltrati nell'organizzazione mafiosa. Tra questi l’agente Calogero Zucchetto, con cui spesso svolgeva indagini e pedinamenti in vespa per le strade di Palermo.

Era convinto che, per sconfiggere la mafia, le istituzioni dovessero impegnarsi nell'educazione alla legalità, soprattutto per le nuove generazioni e per questo amava andare nelle scuole a parlare con gli studenti.

Cassarà fu uno stretto collaboratore del giudice Giovanni Falcone e le sue indagini contribuirono all'istruzione del primo maxiprocesso.

Fu ucciso (insieme all’agente della Squadra Mobile Roberto Antiochia) sotto casa, in Viale Croce Rossa 81, il 6 Agosto 1985. Morì tra le braccia di sua moglie Laura. Aveva 37 anni.
it.CassaraGeofenceAlert: Sei in prossimità di viale della Croce Rossa, qua è avvenuto l’attentato al vice questore di Palermo Antonino "Ninni" Cassarà e dell'agente della Squadra Mobile Roberto Antiochia.

it.ChinniciBodyguardBartolottaDescription: Salvatore Bartolotta nasce a Castrofilippo (Ag)  il 3 marzo 1935. Giovanissimo manifestò la sua intenzione di arruolarsi nell'Arma dei Carabinieri e dopo un breve servizio nelle città di Caltanissetta e Cefalù, venne assegnato definitivamente al Nucleo Investigativo presso la Caserma Carini di Palermo. Alla fine degli anni settanta fu assegnato alla scorta del giudice Rocco Chinnici.La vita di Bartolotta viene spezzata tragicamente da un’ autobomba diretta al giudice Rocco Chinnici il 29 luglio 1983 in via Pipitone Federico a Palermo. Con lui muoiono anche il  maresciallo Mario Trapassi, che, con Bartolotta faceva da scorta a Chinnici, e  Stefano Li Sacchi, il portiere dello stabile in cui risiedeva il giudice. Lascia la moglie e quattro figli.
it.ChinniciBodyguardLiSacchiDescription: Stefano Li Sacchi nasce il 2 giugno 1923 a Geraci Siculo, ( Pa). Si sposa nel gennaio del 1951 e si trasferisce a Palermo dove inizia a lavorare come portiere. Il 29 luglio 1983 una Fiat 127 imbottita di esplosivo, davanti all’abitazione del giudice Rocco Chinnici in via Pipitone Federico dove lavorava, esplode uccidendolo insieme al giudice ed ai due carabinieri di scorta, Maresciallo Mario Trapassi e Appuntato Salvatore Bartolotta.  Il corpo dell’uomo, ricordato per la sua gentilezza con tutti e la sua devozione nei confronti del giudice, viene scaraventato a decine di metri di distanza dallo scoppio.
it.ChinniciBodyguardLiSacchiName: Stefano Li Sacchi (Il portiere dello stabile)
it.ChinniciBodyguardTrapassiDescription:
Mario Trapassi nasce a Palermo l’8 dicembre 1950. Ragazzo serio e determinato, si arruola nell’Arma frequentando la Scuola Sottufficiali di Velletri e di Firenze.

Dopo il matrimonio chiede di essere trasferito a Palermo.

Si fa assegnare alla scorta di Paolo Borsellino, e, appena viene eletto Consigliere Capo del Tribunale di Palermo, Rocco Chinnici, gli viene assegnata la guida della sua scorta.

Muore, insieme all’appuntato Mario Bartolotta ed al portiere dello stabile Stefano Li Sacchi, il 29 luglio 1983 con un’ auto bomba, in Via Pipitone Federico, a Palermo diretta al giudice Rocco Chinnici. Lascia la moglie e quattro figli.
it.ChinniciDescription:
Rocco Chinnici nasce a Misilmeri nel 1925. Era un magistrato, sposato e padre di tre figli.

Nel 1979 diede una svolta nel contrasto alla mafia: indagò sui fondi erogati dalla Regione, mise sotto la lente gli intoccabili cugini esattori Ignazio e Nino Salvo e riaprì il caso Impastato, della sua morte dichiarò: “E’ come se avessero ucciso mio figlio”.

Fu il giudice che ebbe l'idea di istituire un pool. Entrarono a far parte della sua "squadra" alcuni giovani magistrati fra i quali Giuseppe Di Lello, Giovanni Falcone e Paolo Borsellino.

Credeva nel coinvolgimento dei giovani nella lotta contro la mafia, fu il primo magistrato a recarsi nelle scuole per parlare agli studenti della mafia e del pericolo della droga.

È stato ucciso con un’autobomba, -una Fiat 126 verde comodamente parcheggiata, durante la notte, davanti alla sua abitazione in via Pipitone Federico,59 a Palermo, imbottita con 50 chili di tritolo - il 29 luglio 1983 ... unico sopravvissuto Giovanni Paparcuri. Titolarono i giornali: «Palermo come Beirut».
it.ChinniciGeofenceAlert: Sei in prossimità di via Giuseppe Pipitone Federico 59, qua è avvenuto l’attentato al giudice Rocco Chinnici, con la scorta Mario Trapassi, Salvatore Bartolotta e il portiere Stefano Li Sacchi.
it.CostaDescription:
Nasce a Caltanissetta, il 1 marzo 1916 e si laurea in Giurisprudenza a Palermo. Vinto il concorso in Magistratura, si arruola come Ufficiale nell'aviazione. Finita la guerra lavora prima al Tribunale di Roma e poi a Caltanissetta dove svolge la maggior parte della Sua attività di Magistrato, da Sostituto Procuratore e da Procuratore Capo.

Sin dagli anni sessanta intuisce che la mafia aveva subito una radicale mutazione, annidandosi nei gangli vitali della pubblica amministrazione, controllandone appalti, assunzioni e gestione. Inutilmente richiama l'attenzione delle massime autorità sul fatto che unʼefficace lotta alla mafia imponeva la predisposizione di strumenti legislativi, che consentissero di indagare sui patrimoni dei presunti mafiosi e colpirli.

Nel gennaio del 1978 la sua nomina a Procuratore Capo di Palermo fu immediatamente contrastata, tantʼè che fu immesso nelle funzioni solo nel luglio successivo.

Subito si cercò di sottoporlo ad un serrato controllo, costringendolo ad un deciso chiarimento all'interno dell'ufficio stesso. Avvia una serie di delicatissime indagini nell'ambito delle quali tenta di penetrare i santuari patrimoniali della mafia. Nell'ambito di una di queste, qualcuno ritenne di poterlo fermare ponendolo in "minoranza" ma non fu sufficiente: firmò in prima persona i mandati di cattura contestati.
Sufficiente a scatenare la vendetta mafiosa fu, invece, divulgare tale circostanza, come sosterrà Sciascia dopo la sua morte.

Per queste indagini il 6 agosto 1980, mentre passeggiava da solo, rimase vittima di un agguato mafioso, tesogli nel centro di Palermo. Nessuno è stato condannato per la sua morte.

Unico magistrato palermitano cui erano state assegnate auto blindata e scorta, non se ne serviva, perché avrebbe messo a rischio chi era impegnato nelle medesime indagini: non voleva che qualcuno rischiasse la vita per difenderlo ed infine credeva che la sicurezza di un Magistrato risiede nella certezza che, ucciso lui, il successore proseguirà la sua azione.
it.CostaGeofenceAlert: Sei in prossimità di via Cavour, qua è avvenuto l’attentato al Procuratore Capo di Palermo Gaetano Costa.
it.CostaSpeakerDescription: con il racconto di <font color='#e75c06'>Donatella Finocchiaro</font>
it.DallaChiesaBodyguardRussoDescription:
Domenico Russo nacque a Santa Maria Capua Vetere (CE) il 27 dicembre del 1950.

Era un Agente di Polizia e gli fu dato il compito di fare da scorta personale al Generale Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa in quei 100 giorni in cui fu Prefetto di Palermo.

La sera del 3 settembre del 1982 era alla guida della Alfetta di servizio che seguiva la A112 guidata dal Prefetto Dalla Chiesa che era in compagnia della moglie Emanuela Setti Carraro come era sua sovente abitudine.

In via Isidoro Carini, a Palermo, la A112 del Generale fu affiancata da due sicari che falciarono a raffiche di kalashnikov Dalla Chiesa e la giovane moglie.

Russo fu raggiunto da un altro killer che gli esplose contro diversi colpi di pistola che lo ferirono gravemente, tentò di reagire ma senza successo.

Morì il 15 settembre successivo dopo una lunga agonia.

Lascia moglie e due figli piccoli.

Gli fu riconosciuta la Medaglia d’Oro al Valor Civile.
it.DallaChiesaDescription:
Carlo Alberto Dalla Chiesa nasce a Saluzzo, in Piemonte, il 27 settembre 1920.
Nel 1942 dopo avere combattuto in Montenegro entra nell'Arma dei Carabinieri. Comanda la tenenza di San Benedetto del Tronto, dove si unisce alle bande partigiane durante la Resistenza. Nel 1945 sposa Dora Fabbo, conosciuta da ragazzo durante il periodo trascorso a Bari. Da lei avrà tre figli.

Successivamente presta servizio a Casoria, a Firenze, a Corleone, a Como, Milano, Roma, Torino, di nuovo a Milano e poi a Palermo, dal 1966 al 1973.

Nel 1973 diviene Comandante della Regione Militare di Nord-Ovest e nello stesso periodo crea una struttura, "il nucleo speciale antiterrorismo" ottenendo importanti successi nella lotta contro le Brigate Rosse.

Nel febbraio del 1978 Dalla Chiesa perde la moglie Dora, per il Generale un durissimo colpo. Nell’agosto del 1978, dopo il sequestro e l’omicidio dell’On. Aldo Moro, viene incaricato di guidare la lotta al terrorismo sul territorio nazionale.

Il 16 dicembre 1981 viene promosso Vice Comandante Generale dell'Arma e, nel marzo 1982, viene nominato Prefetto di Palermo, dove viene inviato d’urgenza il giorno stesso dell’uccisione dell’ On.le Pio La Torre (30 aprile 1982). L’obiettivo è di ottenere da lui contro Cosa Nostra gli stessi risultati brillanti ottenuti contro le Brigate Rosse. Dalla Chiesa accetta l’incarico chiarendo che solo la concessione di poteri speciali potrà assicurare il successo della missione affidatagli.

Naturalmente ciò non avviene, e appena cento giorni dopo il suo arrivo a Palermo, il 3 settembre 1982, di sera, mentre è alla guida di una A 112 con la giovane moglie, Emanuela Setti Carraro, scortato dall’autista Domenico Russo, viene affiancato da una Bmw che esplode centinaia di proiettili uccidendo sul colpo lui e la moglie. Contemporaneamente l’Agente Russo viene affiancato da una motocicletta che lo ferisce a morte.

Subito dopo tali efferati omicidi, che sconvolgono la pubblica opinione, qualcuno lascia nei luoghi dell’eccidio un cartello con la seguente scritta "qui è morta la speranza dei palermitani onesti".
